_comment: Instrument Tier 2 — 26 severity questions (21 path-attached + 4 always-on + 1 derived) and their conditionals. SPEC §3.1, G-45: the rubric anchor IS the option; a person never picks a bare band word. FR-7: a band may be derived from a fact through a declared mapping — data, never code. Four conditional kinds per FR-8: severity_fired, always_fired, cross_tier, nested.

severity_questions.text: How much of our environment can the third party reach once they are in?
severity_questions.help: Answer for the widest access any one of their people or systems holds, not the typical case.

anchors.low: One system, read-only, and only the records they need to do the job.
anchors.medium: One system with the ability to change data, or several systems read-only.
anchors.high: Several systems, or the ability to change configuration, or access to data belonging to customers other than the ones they support.

severity_questions.text: If the third party lost or exposed the data we give them, what would the consequence be?
severity_questions.help: Think about the people in the data and the business, not about the vendor's embarrassment.

anchors.low: Information that is already public, or aggregated so no individual or deal is identifiable.
anchors.medium: Internal business information, or personal details that would be uncomfortable but not harmful to disclose.
anchors.high: Information that could cause a person real harm, or that would breach a regulatory or contractual obligation on disclosure.

severity_questions.text: How well do we know who sits behind the third party?
severity_questions.help: The suppliers your supplier depends on. If you cannot name them, that is the answer.

anchors.low: We hold a current list of their suppliers, and the contract requires them to tell us before it changes.
anchors.medium: We know the main ones, but the list is not maintained and changes reach us late or not at all.
anchors.high: We do not know who they depend on, or they are entitled to change it without telling us.

severity_questions.text: What happens to the business if this third party stops delivering tomorrow?
severity_questions.help: Assume no notice. Answer for what the business feels, not for what the contract says.

anchors.low: We could switch, absorb it manually, or wait — no customer would notice.
anchors.medium: A visible degradation for days, with a manual workaround that holds for a while.
anchors.high: A process stops. Customers or regulators would notice, and there is no workaround that holds.

severity_questions.text: How well does the contract carry our requirements?
severity_questions.help: Whether the paperwork obliges them to do the things you are about to be asked about.

anchors.low: A current signed agreement with our standard security, privacy and audit terms in it.
anchors.medium: An agreement exists but predates our current standard terms, or some clauses were negotiated away.
anchors.high: No agreement yet, or their terms rather than ours, or nobody has read it against our requirements.

severity_questions.text: How much does the delivery location change the risk?
severity_questions.help: Consider legal reach, the ability to audit, and whether local law could compel access to our data.

anchors.low: A country we already operate in, with an established legal footing and adequacy for data transfers.
anchors.medium: A country we have delivered from before, with transfer safeguards in place but limited ability to inspect on site.
anchors.high: A country we have no presence in, where we cannot practically audit, or where local law could compel access to our data.

severity_questions.text: How far can the AI act before a person sees what it did?
severity_questions.help: The most consequential thing it can do on its own — not the typical thing.

anchors.low: It only suggests. Nothing happens until a person chooses to act on it.
anchors.medium: It acts, but only in reversible ways, and a person reviews the record shortly afterwards.
anchors.high: It acts on its own in ways that reach a customer, move money, or change a record that others rely on, and review is after the fact or absent.

severity_questions.text: How much do we know about the model we are relying on?
severity_questions.help: Where it came from, who can change it, and whether we would notice if it changed.

anchors.low: A named model and version from a supplier with published terms, pinned so it cannot change without us choosing to move.
anchors.medium: A named commercial model that the supplier may update, with release notes we could read if we looked.
anchors.high: We cannot name the model or its version, or it sits inside a product we cannot inspect, or it can change under us silently.

severity_questions.text: What could be exposed through what the model is given at the point of use?
severity_questions.help: Prompts, retrieved documents and records sent with a request. Include anything the supplier could retain or use for their own training.

anchors.low: Only information that is already public, or data with identifiers removed before it is sent.
anchors.medium: Internal business information, under terms that prohibit the supplier retaining or training on it.
anchors.high: Personal or confidential information, or we cannot confirm the supplier will not retain or train on what we send.

severity_questions.text: What is the consequence if the AI is confidently wrong?
severity_questions.help: Assume a plausible, well-written, wrong answer that nobody catches.

anchors.low: A person would notice immediately and the cost is a moment of their time.
anchors.medium: It could reach a colleague and be acted on, but the error would surface within the normal course of work.
anchors.high: It could reach a customer or a regulator, drive a decision about a person, or be indistinguishable from a correct answer.

severity_questions.text: How well could someone see what the AI is doing and stop it?
severity_questions.help: Both halves matter — being able to see, and being able to stop.

anchors.low: Every use is logged with its inputs and outputs, a named owner watches it, and a person can turn it off in minutes.
anchors.medium: Use is logged and someone owns it, but nobody reviews routinely and turning it off needs a change.
anchors.high: We could not reconstruct what it did, or nobody is named as owning it, or stopping it means an outage for something else.

severity_questions.text: How intrusive is this use of people's information, from their point of view?
severity_questions.help: Judge it as the person in the data would, not as the project would.

anchors.low: Exactly what they gave it to us for, and they would expect it.
anchors.medium: A related use they would probably accept if it were explained, but were not told about up front.
anchors.high: A use they would be surprised or unhappy to learn about, or one that produces a decision about them.

severity_questions.text: Roughly how many people's information is involved?
severity_questions.help: An order of magnitude is enough. This one you answer as a fact, and the band is worked out from it.

derivation.reason: The band comes from the number of people you told us are involved.

severity_questions.text: How central is the specially protected information to what this activity does?
severity_questions.help: Incidental presence still counts, but it is not the same as building the activity around it.

anchors.low: It could appear incidentally in free text, and the activity does not act on it.
anchors.medium: It is present and used, but only to do the thing the person asked for.
anchors.high: The activity is built around it — it drives a decision, a score, or who gets what.

severity_questions.text: How well protected is the transfer out of the country?
severity_questions.help: What legally and practically protects the data once it is somewhere else.

anchors.low: To a country recognised as offering equivalent protection, under a current agreement.
anchors.medium: To a country without that recognition, but with approved contractual safeguards signed and a transfer assessment done.
anchors.high: No safeguards in place yet, or we do not know which countries it reaches, or local law could compel access.

severity_questions.text: How clearly is it decided when this information gets deleted?
severity_questions.help: Deleted for real, including from backups and from any copy the third party holds.

anchors.low: A retention period is set, it is enforced automatically, and it covers every copy including the vendor's.
anchors.medium: A retention period is set but deletion is manual, or it does not yet cover backups or vendor copies.
anchors.high: Nothing is decided, or the answer is that we keep it indefinitely.

severity_questions.text: How well could we answer a person asking what we hold about them?
severity_questions.help: Including correcting it, and deleting it if they are entitled to that.

anchors.low: We can find, correct, export and delete an individual's records within the required time, in this system.
anchors.medium: We could do it, but it needs someone manual and would take real effort inside the deadline.
anchors.high: We could not reliably find everything we hold about one person, or a vendor copy would be missed.

severity_questions.text: How well controlled is privileged access to this system?
severity_questions.help: Privileged means being able to change the system or read all of its data.

anchors.low: Named individual accounts only, issued through a vault, time-limited, with every session recorded.
anchors.medium: Named accounts with strong authentication, but standing rather than time-limited, and sessions are not recorded.
anchors.high: Accounts shared between people, or credentials that do not expire, or nobody could list who holds privileged access today.

severity_questions.text: How exposed is the system at its boundary?
severity_questions.help: What an unauthenticated stranger on the internet can reach.

anchors.low: Nothing is reachable without authenticating, and it sits behind a gateway that filters and rate-limits.
anchors.medium: A login page and documented APIs are public, behind a gateway, with monitoring in place.
anchors.high: Administrative interfaces, file uploads or unauthenticated endpoints are reachable from the internet, or nobody has confirmed what is exposed.

severity_questions.text: How well would we be able to reconstruct what happened after an incident?
severity_questions.help: Assume you are asked, six months later, who accessed a particular record and when.

anchors.low: Access and change logs go to a central store, are retained for the required period, and cannot be altered by the people they record.
anchors.medium: Logs exist and are retained, but they stay local to the system and nobody watches them.
anchors.high: Logging is partial or absent, retained for days, or the people with privileged access could remove their own traces.

severity_questions.text: How confident are we that we could actually get this back?
severity_questions.help: Confidence should come from a restore that has been performed, not from a backup job that reports success.

anchors.low: Backups are taken, held separately, and a restore has been tested within the last year against the recovery time the business expects.
anchors.medium: Backups are taken and held separately, but a restore has never been tested end to end.
anchors.high: We rely on the vendor's word, or backups are in the same place as the system, or nobody knows what the recovery time really is.

severity_questions.text: How controlled is the path from a change to production?
severity_questions.help: Who can put a change live, and what stands between them and doing it.

anchors.low: Every change is reviewed by someone else, tested automatically, and released through a pipeline nobody can bypass.
anchors.medium: Changes are reviewed and released through a pipeline, but someone can deploy directly in an emergency.
anchors.high: Changes can go live without another person seeing them, or releases are manual, or there is no record of what was deployed when.

severity_questions.text: How critical is this activity to the business?
severity_questions.help: Asked of every activity, whatever else it touches.

anchors.low: A convenience. If it stopped, the affected team would work around it and nobody outside would know.
anchors.medium: An important process. If it stopped, a business unit would feel it within days.
anchors.high: Something the business runs on. If it stopped, customers, revenue or a regulatory obligation would be affected immediately.

severity_questions.text: How broadly will this be used?
severity_questions.help: Reach, not importance.

anchors.low: One team, or a pilot with a named handful of users.
anchors.medium: A business unit, or several teams across the organisation.
anchors.high: The whole organisation, or anyone outside it.

severity_questions.text: Who sees what this produces?
severity_questions.help: The furthest the output travels, including indirectly.

anchors.low: Only the person who asked for it.
anchors.medium: Colleagues, who may act on it as part of their work.
anchors.high: Customers, the public, a regulator, or an external partner.

severity_questions.text: If this went badly wrong, how material would it be?
severity_questions.help: One bad day, at the worst plausible end. Financial, regulatory or reputational.

anchors.low: Absorbed inside a team's budget and forgotten in a week.
anchors.medium: A cost or a complaint that a business unit would have to explain.
anchors.high: A loss, a regulatory notification, or press coverage that reaches the executive.

conditionals.text: How does the third party's access get removed when one of their people leaves?
conditionals.help: Only asked because their reach is Medium or wider. If you do not know their process, hand this off rather than guessing.

options.label: Automatically, from their own joiner-leaver process
They tell us and we remove it
It comes out at the next access review

conditionals.text: How long could a leaver's access stay live?
conditionals.help: Asked because removal depends on a review rather than on their leaving. An estimate is fine.

conditionals.text: What is the largest action the AI can take without a person approving it?
conditionals.help: Asked because it acts in other systems on its own. Describe the limit as it is configured today, not as intended.

conditionals.text: Does the supplier's agreement prohibit them retaining or training on what we send?
conditionals.help: Asked whenever the model sees our data, whatever the severity. This is a fact about the contract, not a judgement.

options.label: Yes, and it is in writing
Their published terms say so, but we have no specific agreement

conditionals.text: Which countries will the information reach?
conditionals.help: Every country where it is stored or viewed from. Recorded for the privacy office — it does not change your severity.

conditionals.text: How often is privileged access reviewed and reconfirmed?
conditionals.help: Asked because privileged access is Medium or looser. Reviewed means somebody confirmed each person still needs it.

conditionals.text: When was a restore last performed successfully?
conditionals.help: Asked because recovery confidence is Medium or lower. A backup job reporting success is not a restore.

conditionals.text: How is a child's age established, and who consents on their behalf?
conditionals.help: Asked because children's information is involved and the use is Medium or more central.
